THIS MFA FILED U/S. 173(1) OF MV ACT, BY THE ADVOCATE FOR APPELLANT PRAYING TO a) EXERCISE ITS APPELLATE JURISDICTION, CALL FOR THE ENTIRE LOWER COURT RECORDS AND MODIFY THE JUDGEMENT AND AWARD DATED-11.02.2019 PASSED BY THE LEARNED II ADDL.
SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT AT KALABURAGI IN MVC NO.625/2014 BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT FROM RS.2,04,000/- TO RS.15,00,000/-, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ARGUMENTS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the II Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.625/2014 dated 11.02.2019.
2. Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
On 23-12-2013 at about 12.30 P.M., near to the land of one Channaveer of village Nagoor, on Gulbarga Revanasiddeshwar Hill Temple road, petitioner along with Prashantkumar Talikoti were proceeding on Motorcycle bearing No.KA-32/Y-4974,
petitioner was a pillion rider.
The rider of the Motorcycle drove it in a rash and negligent manner, due to skidding of Motorcycle, petitioner fell down on ground.
As a result, petitioner sustained grievous injuries and fracture.
Immediately she was shifted to hospital, she spent Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment and she required a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- for further medical expenses.
Hence, she preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.

5. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 though appeared through counsel but not filed counter/written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.2,04,000/-.

sentences.text: 2 8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
9. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the owner/insurer had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.

12. Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned, injuries show that claimant had suffered permanent disability to the extent of 10.66% and to prove the same the claimant has produced the disability certificate at Ex. P-9.
13.

The claimant was working as Assistant at Stop N Shop and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month,
but she has not produced any evidence to prove the said income.
Hence, the Tribunal has taken the income of claimant at Rs.6,000/- per month.
However, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2013, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.7,000/- p.m.
The claimant was aged about 30 years at the time of the accident and the multiplier that would be applicable for her age group is '17'.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,57,080/- (Rs.7,500/- x 12 x 17 x 11%) on account of 'loss of future income'.

14. Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re-determined and re-calculated as under:-

In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the II Addl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi in MVC.No.625/2014 dated 11.02.2019 is modified.

per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of two months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
